question: Who was the first Indian to qualify for Covenanted service?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Satyendra Nath Tagore.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Satyendra Nath Tagore was the first Indian to qualify for Covenanted service.**
 
• **He cleared the Indian Civil Service (ICS) examination in 1863 and joined the Bengal Presidency Civil Service.**
 
• **He was a member of Bramho Samaj. **
 
• Tagore was a prominent member of the Tagore family and was the elder brother of Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Covenanted service was a term used to describe the higher ranks of the Indian Civil Service, which was the administrative arm of the British Raj in India.
 
• Gopal Krishna Gokhale was a member of the Indian National Congress and advocated for constitutional reforms and self-rule for India.
 
 
• He was also a mentor to Mahatma Gandhi.
 
 
 
• Subhash Chandra Bose was a radical nationalist leader.
 
 
• He formed the Indian National Army to fight against the British during World War II.
 
 
 
• **Surendra Nath Banerjee was a prominent Indian nationalist leader who founded the Indian National Association.**
 
 
• **It later became the Indian National Congress.**
